h: Walls, gardens and the city on your doorstep
p: An hour or two is about right for York Art Gallery, and the great thing is where it sits. Exhibition Square is a little cultural hub in its own right, and it's one of the best jumping-off points in the city.

Look out for the statue of William Etty in front of the gallery. He was a York-born painter famous in his day, and he campaigned to save the city walls from being knocked down. So it's fitting that Bootham Bar, one of the old gateways, is right next to the square. Climb up here for a stretch of the city walls, heading round towards Monk Bar for some of the finest views of York Minster you'll find anywhere.

Just round the corner, Museum Gardens is a lovely green space with the ruins of St Mary's Abbey, squirrels darting about and the Yorkshire Museum, which is well worth a visit for its archaeology and natural history. On a sunny day it's the perfect spot to sit with a sandwich.

From there, the rest of York opens up. The Minster is a few minutes' walk away, the Shambles and its little shops are a short stroll beyond, and the riverside along the Ouse is lovely for an evening wander. If the family wants something completely different, the National Railway Museum is a walk away near the station, and Jorvik Viking Centre brings the city's Viking past to life. York rewards those who wander, so don't overplan.
